portInfo.description: Dover makes its geography visible immediately: a working Channel harbour below a castle and chalk cliffs. Yet a sea view is not a safe pedestrian route. The port, town and cliff-top visitor facilities sit at different levels, so plan a permitted port exit and the uphill transfer before booking an attraction. One substantial castle visit often works better than trying to collect distant Kent sights on the same day. This is an editorial recommendation, not an operator excursion promise.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: Confirm the actual terminal in sailing documents. The Port of Dover Cruise brochure (passenger-services matrix) lists a taxi rank at Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, and a regular shuttle bus to the city centre at Terminal 1, Terminal 2 and Berth 4. The same brochure states the shuttle is provided for passengers and/or crew at their own expense, unless the cruise line covers the cost. It also states distance from town centre as 1.4 miles and from the train station as 1.2 miles. These are brochure facilities statements, not a public timetable, fare table or step-free guarantee. For itinerary budgeting, allow an editorial 45 minutes each way between ship and the town or castle, including waiting for the brochure shuttle/taxi and the gate process. Prefer the brochure shuttle or a port-authorised taxi over an unverified pedestrian dock exit. The castle directions and cliff visitor-centre directions must be checked separately; do not navigate to an Eastern Docks ferry entrance. Current shuttle headways, accessible boarding, rail/airport timetables, luggage storage and fares remain unverified beyond the brochure matrix. An embarkation-day train connection requires additional luggage and check-in margin rather than the sightseeing allowances below.
gettingThere.publicTransport: Confirm local transport options with the ship on your call date.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Dover Castle, Castle Hill: allow about three hours for a focused visit rather than promising every tunnel and exhibition. Check the exact date's opening and access provisions; a hilltop castle is not automatically a step-free attraction.

White Cliffs visitor centre, Langdon Cliffs, Upper Road: allow 60–90 minutes for a short nearby cliff-top walk and break. Stay on official paths and away from edges. The current page says Fan Bay Deep Shelter and Emplacement are closed until March 2027; do not include them in a winter itinerary.
Dover Museum, Market Square: allow an hour for a town-centre indoor option. The municipal page gives different summer and winter Sunday arrangements; check the actual visit date.
Roman Painted House, New Street: allow 45 minutes only when reopening is confirmed. Its current winter closure makes it a future candidate, not a reliable November 2026 stop.

South Foreland Lighthouse, St Margaret's Bay: treat this as a separate extended coastal outing, not a quick addition from the cruise pier. The current official notice says the tower, tearoom, shop and toilets are closed for winter, reopening in March. There is no direct vehicular access: the National Trust describes a two-mile walk from the White Cliffs visitor centre. Confirm reopening, access and return route before setting out. A 90-minute site allowance excludes the substantial approach walk. Exact approach and transfer timing remain unresolved.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: For seven hours, allow 45 minutes to Dover Castle, 180 minutes visiting, 45 minutes for lunch and 45 minutes returning. The remaining 105 minutes is the ship buffer and recovery margin. This deliberately omits the cliffs and London. Book only after the castle calendar and ship arrival window fit together.
thingsToDo.longerCall: For nine hours, reserve 45 minutes to the castle, 150 minutes visiting, 45 minutes for lunch, 45 minutes to the White Cliffs visitor centre, 90 minutes for a short path outing and 60 minutes back. Keep 105 minutes for the ship. Transfers are conservative editorial allowances requiring independent route QA. In poor weather, use a longer castle visit or town museum instead of the cliff segment. An overnight does not make a late return safe without transport and reboarding arrangements.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: The cliffs visible from the ship are not the visitor-centre entrance. Save Upper Road for the National Trust arrival point and confirm the passenger gate before judging any route from its apparent distance.
